entries.title: Automation handover record
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Record ownership, inputs, expected results, failure handling, and the checks another operator needs to support an automation.

entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption

entries.title: Cyber risk assessment and treatment report
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: This report helps a decision-maker understand a risk, choose a treatment, and determine whether the treatment worked. Its structure separates an observed condition from a proposed fix, implementation evidence, and residual risk.

entries.title: Data classification and handling policy
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: This policy defines how the Firm classifies, stores, shares, and disposes of information. It applies to employees, contractors, service providers, and information in electronic, printed, or spoken form.

entries.title: Decision memo: tracking vendor renewals
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: How should a 12-person operations team keep renewal dates, decisions, and ownership visible without creating a custom application that nobody is prepared to support?

entries.title: Disaster recovery playbook
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Use this playbook with the business continuity plan. The goal is to restore an agreed business capability and verify that people can use it safely. Restoring a file or receiving a successful job status is only part of recovery.

entries.title: Identity and access management policy
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: This policy governs who may access the Firm's systems, how that access is approved, and how it is removed. It covers employees, contractors, administrators, service identities, and third parties.

entries.title: Incident response record
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Use this record to preserve the facts, decisions, actions, and verification associated with an incident. Update it as the investigation changes; identify assumptions and superseded conclusions rather than silently replacing them.

entries.title: Lost or stolen device response procedure
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Use this procedure when a managed phone, tablet, or laptop is reported missing. The priorities are personal safety, protection of information and access, evidence preservation, and restoring the person's ability to work.

entries.title: Runbook: recover a sample document workspace
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Use a dedicated test destination and fictional sample files. Identify an exercise owner, an operator, and a reviewer acting as an ordinary user. Record the selected recovery point, authorized destination, expected objects, and intended access…

entries.title: Software request and approval procedure
entries.readiness: Fictional or adapted example; requires internal adoption
entries.description: Use this procedure for a new subscription, desktop application, browser extension, AI tool, connector, or material expansion of an existing tool. The outcome is a documented decision with a defined scope, followed by verified provisioning or a…

entries.title: Defining portfolio company support
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: Firm IT and portfolio-company IT can collaborate without sharing the same authority or environment. Before offering support, define what is being provided, who owns the decision, and where the resulting information belongs.

entries.title: Joiners role changes and departures
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: Access is a lifecycle, not a one-time setup task. A VC firm's employees, contractors, advisers, temporary staff, and external collaborators may each need a different sponsor, data boundary, and end date.

entries.title: Managing a technology vendor through its lifecycle
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: A vendor review should answer whether the service fits the intended work, what the firm will depend on, and how it can leave. Keep those questions alive after purchase.

entries.title: Running the VC IT function
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: The first job is to make ownership visible. A small firm may outsource support, security monitoring, fund administration, and application delivery to different providers. Someone inside the firm still needs to decide priorities, accept risk,…

entries.title: Technology support for fund and investor operations
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: The useful starting point is the workflow between people and systems. A correct application configuration does not by itself ensure that the right investor receives the right document or that a changed payment instruction is independently…

entries.title: The first 90 days of a VC IT review
entries.readiness: Proposed operating guidance
entries.description: This is an illustrative sequence for an incoming IT owner or a firm improving its operating model. Adjust it to urgent risks, staffing, and business deadlines. Calendar milestones are planning aids, not permission to defer a known serious issue.

entries.title: Access review preparation
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Prepare a review queue by matching human application grants to an authoritative workforce snapshot. This helps an IT operator separate routine decisions from leaver access, unknown identities, dormant grants, privilege, and missing ownership.…

entries.title: Automation result review
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Compare an intended set of record IDs with an observed set. This is a small component of an acceptance review, useful after a migration or automation run.

entries.title: Backup and recovery evidence review
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Compare supplied recovery evidence with each workload's objectives. This separates the time a backup job finished from the age of the data it protects, and separates backup evidence from measured restore performance.

entries.title: Joiner, mover, and leaver completeness review
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Check lifecycle cases against a declared task catalog and case-specific additions. The useful question is whether approved scope has corresponding completion evidence, including removal of prior access after a move and handover after a…

entries.title: Operations brief
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Collect service observations into one reviewable draft, keeping incomplete evidence and unassigned ownership visible.

entries.title: SaaS license reconciliation
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Compare purchased seats, application assignments, workforce status, and usage to prepare a license review. The output separates spare capacity from unused or departed-user candidates and keeps technical accounts out of automatic reclamation.

entries.title: Vendor renewal triage
entries.readiness: Local logic checked; n8n runtime trial pending
entries.description: Turn a vendor register into a dated review queue. A renewal 60 days away can already have a missed cancellation deadline, so this workflow orders work by the supplied notice period. It keeps business dependency, decision evidence, exit…

entries.title: Build-versus-buy review

entries.description: Compare building, buying, and combining tools through ownership, operating costs, risk, and a bounded trial.

entries.title: Document sanitization
